label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.11 a.3…: Two distinct first movers moved by none would differ…
locator: I q.11 a.3 co., second proof: Si ergo essent plures dii, oporteret eos differre. Aliquid ergo conveniret uni, quod non alteri
interpretation: Scoped to the plural hypothesis, the weakest reading the argument uses: distinct first movers moved by none would differ, something belonging to one and not to the other, read as one being in act in a respect in which the other is not. It applies the general principle that what are many differ only to first movers, and it does not assume that they are perfect.
